## 1\. The exact Maxwell–Stefan entropy metric

Let

\[
f_-=\min_{i\ne j}f_{ij},\qquad
f_+=\max_{i\ne j}f_{ij},\qquad
\lambda=\frac1{f_+}.
\]

All three quantities are computable positive rationals.

For positive concentrations, write

\[
J_i=c_i v_i,\qquad \sum_i c_iv_i=0.
\]

The friction equations become

\[
-\nabla\log c_i
=\sum_{j\ne i}f_{ij}c_j(v_i-v_j).
\]

Define the weighted friction operator

\[
(L_cv)_i=\sum_{j\ne i}f_{ij}c_j(v_i-v_j).
\]

Its quadratic form satisfies

\[
\begin{aligned}
\langle v,L_cv\rangle_c
&=\frac12\sum_{i,j}f_{ij}c_ic_j|v_i-v_j|^2,\\
f_-\sum_i c_i|v_i|^2
&\leq\langle v,L_cv\rangle_c
\leq f_+\sum_i c_i|v_i|^2,
\end{aligned}
\]

where \(\langle v,w\rangle_c=\sum_i c_i v_i\cdot w_i\), and the inequalities use \(\sum_i c_iv_i=0\)\.

Thus the friction operator is uniformly positive in its natural weighted tangent space, with bounds independent of the concentrations' distance from the simplex boundary.

For a smooth positive solution, incompressible advection cancels exactly from the relative-entropy balance\:

\[
\frac{dH}{dt}=-\mathcal D(t),
\]

where

\[
\mathcal D(t)=
\frac12\int_{\mathbb T^3}
\sum_{i,j}f_{ij}c_ic_j|v_i-v_j|^2\,dx.
\]

Spectral comparison of \(L_c\) gives two useful estimates\:

\[
\boxed{
\sum_i\|\nabla c_i\|_2^2
\leq f_+\mathcal D,
\qquad
\sum_i\|J_i\|_2^2
\leq f_-^{-1}\mathcal D.
}
\tag{1}
\]

The stronger Fisher-information bound is

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal D\geq
\frac1{f_+}
\sum_i\int_{\mathbb T^3}
\frac{|\nabla c_i|^2}{c_i}\,dx
=
\frac4{f_+}\sum_i\|\nabla\sqrt{c_i}\|_2^2.
}
\tag{2}
\]

These estimates are valid by approximation when concentrations vanish.

## 2\. Entropy and concentration fluctuations are globally comparable

Set

\[
p_i=\bar c_i,\qquad u_i=c_i-p_i.
\]

Because \(0\leq c_i\leq1\) and \(p_i\geq m\),

\[
\boxed{
\frac12\|u\|_{L^2(\mathbb T^3;\mathbb R^N)}^2
\leq H(c|p)
\leq\frac1m\|u\|_{L^2(\mathbb T^3;\mathbb R^N)}^2.
}
\tag{3}
\]

The upper bound follows from \(\log x\leq x-1\); the lower bound follows from the scalar entropy Hessian \(1/c_i\geq1\)\.

Importantly, no pointwise lower bound \(c_i\geq a>0\) is required.

## 3\. A robust nonlinear mixing comparison

Let \(S_\lambda(t)\) be the scalar semigroup generated by

\[
\lambda\Delta-b\cdot\nabla.
\]

Fix a positive time \(\tau\)\. Compare the nonlinear concentration fluctuation \(u\) against

\[
z_i(t)=S_\lambda(t)u_i(0).
\]

Put \(w=u-z\)\. The equations imply

\[
\partial_t w+b\cdot\nabla w
=\lambda\Delta w-\nabla\cdot(J+\lambda\nabla c).
\]

The standard \(L^2\) energy estimate and (1) give

\[
\begin{aligned}
\|w(\tau)\|_2^2
&\leq\frac1\lambda
\int_0^\tau\|J+\lambda\nabla c\|_2^2\,dt\\
&\leq
2\left(1+\frac{f_+}{f_-}\right)
\big[H(c(0)|p)-H(c(\tau)|p)\big].
\end{aligned}
\]

Define

\[
\boxed{\Gamma=2\left(1+\frac{f_+}{f_-}\right).}
\]

Suppose the scalar mixer satisfies

\[
\|S_\lambda(\tau)P_0\|_{2\to2}\leq q.
\]

Then

\[
\boxed{
\|u(\tau)\|_2
\leq
q\sqrt{2H(c(0)|p)}
+\sqrt{\Gamma\,[H(c(0)|p)-H(c(\tau)|p)]}.
}
\tag{4}
\]

This is a genuinely nonlinear comparison. It treats the full cross-diffusion flux as an uncertain dissipative medium and pays for its departure from scalar diffusion using the actual entropy loss.

It does not replace the Maxwell–Stefan matrix by a scalar coefficient or assume that its symmetric part is positive in Euclidean coordinates.

## 4\. An explicit uniform entropy contraction

Choose

\[
q=\frac m{16},
\qquad
\boxed{
\delta=\frac{m}{32(1+f_+/f_-)}
=\frac m{16\Gamma}.
}
\]

Let \(H_0=H(c(0)|p)\), \(H_\tau=H(c(\tau)|p)\)\.

If \(H_\tau\leq H_0/2\), then certainly

\[
H_\tau\leq(1-\delta)H_0.
\]

Otherwise, put \(h=H_\tau/H_0>1/2\)\. Equations (3)–(4) imply

\[
\sqrt{mh}
\leq \sqrt2q+\sqrt{\Gamma(1-h)}.
\]

Since \(m\leq1\) and \(q=m/16\), rearranging yields

\[
1-h\geq\frac m{16\Gamma}=\delta.
\]

Thus, in both cases,

\[
\boxed{
H(c(\tau)|p)\leq(1-\delta)H(c(0)|p).
}
\tag{5}
\]

The contraction is uniform in \(N\), the initial spatial profile and the solution's future derivatives. The constants depend only on the supplied friction data and \(m\)\.

## 5\. Arbitrarily prescribed entropy decay

Choose the rational time

\[
\boxed{\tau=\frac{\delta}{2\chi}.}
\]

Use the accepted polynomial-resource scalar construction to produce one stationary rational-trigonometric divergence-free velocity \(b\) satisfying

\[
\boxed{
\|e^{\tau(\lambda\Delta-b\cdot\nabla)}P_0\|_{2\to2}
\leq\frac m{16}.
}
\tag{6}
\]

Applying (5) successively on intervals of length \(\tau\), and using entropy monotonicity between their endpoints, gives

\[
H(c(t)|p)
\leq (1-\delta)^{\lfloor t/\tau\rfloor}H(c_0|p).
\]

Because \(-\log(1-\delta)\geq\delta\),

\[
\boxed{
H(c(t)|\bar c)
\leq
\frac1{1-\delta}e^{-2\chi t}H(c_0|\bar c)
\leq
\frac1{1-\delta}e^{-\chi t}H(c_0|\bar c).
}
\tag{7}
\]

Therefore the entropy-decay prefactor can be chosen explicitly as

\[
\boxed{C=(1-\delta)^{-1}<2.}
\]

The velocity is computed from rational inputs \((\lambda,\tau,m/16)\)\. Its construction costs are consequently bounded by the accepted scalar primitive's explicit polynomial evaluated on those rational quantities. No new PDE or numerical oracle is required.

**Precisely established scope\:** Equation (7) holds for every global Maxwell–Stefan solution satisfying the simplex constraint, flux relations, and entropy-dissipation inequality, with sufficient weak regularity for the comparison argument. It also holds on every interval of existence of a classical solution.

This proves the requested arbitrary-rate entropy estimate *conditional on global entropy-admissible solvability*\. It does not yet prove global strong solvability.
